title_ar: مشروعية القيام بالتكبير مطلقا بعد سلام الإمام
title_en: The prescribedness of rising with the takbīr in all cases after the imam's salām
body_ar:
القيام بالتكبير في الأوتار بعد سلام الإمام ما حكمه؟

أن الأصل التكبير في كل خفض ورفع لحديث أبي هريرة أن النبي (ص) كان يكبر في كل خفض ورفع، وعلى هذا فإذا سلم الإمام فبقي المأموم في جلسة السلام مسبوقا فعليه أن يقوم بالتكبير مطلقا سواء كان دخل الصلاة على وتر أو شفع، لأن حديث أبي هريرة هذا فيه الإطلاق، وما يذكره الفقهاء من التفصيل بين أن يدخل الصلاة على شفع وبين أن يدخلها على وتر ليس عليه دليل مفصل، وهذا الدليل حاسم لذلك فعلى الإنسان أن يقوم بالتكبير في كل خفض ورفع دائما، لأن هذا الذي كان النبي (ص) يفعله.
body_en:
Rising with the takbīr on the odd-numbered rakʿahs after the imam's salām — what is its ruling?

The base rule (al-aṣl) is the takbīr at every lowering and raising, because of the hadith of Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, upon whom be peace, used to say the takbīr at every lowering and raising. On this basis, when the imam gives the salām and the follower remains in the sitting of the salām as a latecomer (masbūq), he must rise with the takbīr in all cases, whether he entered the prayer on an odd or an even number, because this hadith of Abu Hurayrah is unqualified (muṭlaq). What the jurists mention by way of distinguishing between entering the prayer on an even number and entering it on an odd number has no detailed evidence supporting it, and this evidence is decisive on the point. So a person must rise with the takbīr at every lowering and raising, always, because this is what the Prophet, upon whom be peace, used to do.
translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.

The date shown by the CMS (27 December 2010) is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

The Sheikh gives his own ruling in this text, against the detail drawn by 'the jurists' (al-fuqahāʾ, here the Maliki school's own detailed position). The attribution of the distinction to the jurists and his rejection of it must both remain visible.
'The base rule (al-aṣl)' is the default position from which one departs only on evidence; it is not itself one of the five rulings.
'Odd' and 'even' render witr and shafʿ, here used of the number of rakʿahs the latecomer has caught with the imam, not of the witr prayer.
